important.name: Upgrade step 3 points the TodoCatalog pin at schemas_dir and misses the project's own RepoToDo.schema.json
important.summary:
docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md step 3 of 'Upgrading from 0.7' tells only 'a project that pins TodoCatalog.schema.json under its schemas_dir' to refresh its copy before items carry a keyword. T1 resolves the catalog schema as `todo.catalog_schema` first (default `RepoToDo.schema.json` beside the catalog, used when present) and falls back to `schema_path(...)` (schemas_dir, then the plugin) only when that key is null (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/rules_todo.py:34-35). So the common case, a project keeping `<todo.folder>/RepoToDo.schema.json` or a file named by `todo.catalog_schema`, is left out. Two other documents in this same PR describe the pin correctly: the README TODO keyword paragraph and the new schemas/README.md Migration entry ('todo.catalog_schema, or RepoToDo.schema.json beside the catalog'). A project that follows the release body runs `todo_sync.py keywords` and then gets a T1 finding for every keyworded item. This file is the GitHub release body.

Also (system_shape): This PR widens the CLAUDE.md major-bump rule (CLAUDE.md:125) to 'a schema change that invalidates existing artifacts or pinned copies', and v1.0.0 claims major on the DesignEvolution break alone. Since v0.7.0 (harness 0.65.1), schemas/README.md Migration (lines 342-345) records four more pinned-copy breaks shipped in this release: the freeze ledger (0.69.0, a pinned ActionPlan.schema.json rejects `ledger`), PR_REVIEW 2.3.0 plus the matrix `dispatch_shape` `workflow` (0.71.0: the schema hook rejects `-a` reviews and agent-watcher workflow rows, and `capture -a` refuses the old pin), ActionPlan `refs` (0.79.0: the hook rejects every `--refs` plan), and TodoCatalog `keyword` (0.82.0). docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md Breaking changes (30-42) lists only DesignEvolution, and Upgrading from 0.7 (13-28) covers only DesignEvolution and TodoCatalog. A 0.7 project that pins its review, matrix or plan schema under `schemas_dir` follows the upgrade steps and then hits hook rejections that the release body never names. The `inbox put` keyword refusal is also a behavior break, and it appears only inside step 3.

Also (roast): Step 3 of 'Upgrading from 0.7' tells only a project that pins `TodoCatalog.schema.json` under `schemas_dir` to refresh it. The pin most projects actually carry is the default `todo.catalog_schema`, `RepoToDo.schema.json` beside the catalog, which `config.py:581` resolves whenever the file is present and `rules_todo.py:33-35` validates against ahead of any `schemas_dir` copy. A project on that default follows the guide, runs `todo_sync.py keywords`, and T1 then flags every keyworded item. The schemas README Migration entry this PR adds and the root README both name `RepoToDo.schema.json`, so the release notes are the one place that gets it wrong. The upgrade guide is the page people actually follow.
fix: Reword step 3 to cover every pin T1 reads: 'A project that keeps its own catalog schema (`<todo.folder>/RepoToDo.schema.json`, the file `todo.catalog_schema` names, or `catalogs/TodoCatalog.schema.json` under `schemas_dir` when `todo.catalog_schema` is null): refresh it from the plugin's `catalogs/TodoCatalog.schema.json` (or add the `keyword` property) before any item carries a keyword.'

Add an Upgrading step to docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md: 'A project that pins PR_REVIEW.schema.json, pr_review_invocation_test_matrix.schema.json or ActionPlan.schema.json under schemas_dir: drop the pins or copy the plugin's (schemas README, Migration: 0.69.0, 0.71.0, 0.79.0).' Then list those pinned-copy breaks and the TodoCatalog keyword one as Breaking changes bullets, matching the CLAUDE.md:125 definition.

Alternatively, narrow the CLAUDE.md:125 wording to artifact-invalidating changes only and state in Breaking changes that pinned copies must be refreshed per the schemas README Migration section. The two documents must then agree on which changes are breaking.

Rewrite step 3 to cover both pins: 'A project whose TODO catalog schema is pinned (`RepoToDo.schema.json` beside the catalog, the file `todo.catalog_schema` names, or `catalogs/TodoCatalog.schema.json` under `schemas_dir`): refresh it from the plugin's `catalogs/TodoCatalog.schema.json` (or add the `keyword` property) before any item carries a keyword.' Leave the rest of the step as it is.

important.name: TODO item todo-5v8j is added open and NEEDS_DECISION for work this same PR completes
important.summary:
docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json:4373-4380 adds todo-5v8j (issue #331) as status NEEDS_DECISION with the question 'trim other text to fit under RULES_LIMIT, or raise the 10000-character cap'. The same PR does all four parts of its proposed_change: (1) the mod README layout with What it does, Command, Known limitations and Loading sections, (2) Hooks tables in session-bookmark and pytest-scope, (3) the PROVENANCE row for the shared.css colors (docs/PROVENANCE.md), and (4) the Locked-files rule in HARNESS_RULES.md:124-126. It also settles the decision by trimming: the file is now 9991 characters and the cap is unchanged. docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:83-92 reports the work done. After merge, the catalog and the todo-watch band still ask for a decision that has already been made, and they rank work that has already shipped.

Also (roast): The catalog gains `todo-5v8j` (issue #331) with status `NEEDS_DECISION` and the question 'trim other text to fit under RULES_LIMIT, or raise the 10000-character cap'. This same PR settles all four parts. The mod README layout, the session-bookmark and pytest-scope Hooks tables, the PROVENANCE row and the Locked-files rule all land, and HARNESS_RULES.md was trimmed to 9,991 characters, which answers the question. The release notes even file the work under 'Docs(plugins) ... (issue #331)'. On merge, main's catalog, its counts (`needs_decision` 43) and the snapshot list finished work as an open decision.

Also (docs): docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json:4373 adds todo-5v8j (#331) with status NEEDS_DECISION and the question 'trim other text ... or raise the 10000-character cap'. The same PR does all four parts: it applies the README layout, adds the session-bookmark and pytest-scope Hooks tables and the shared.css PROVENANCE row, and adds the Locked-files rule by trimming HARNESS_RULES.md (9991 characters, under RULES_LIMIT). The release notes (docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:83-92) present this as done. After the merge the catalog and todo-watch will show finished work as open and undecided.

Also (overall): docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json adds todo-5v8j (#331) with status NEEDS_DECISION. Its decision question asks whether to trim HARNESS_RULES.md or raise the cap, and this PR already settles that: the rules file is trimmed to 9991 characters and gains the Locked-files rule. The PR also lands the other three parts of the item, the mod README layout with Known limitations and Loading sections, the session-bookmark and pytest-scope Hooks tables, and the PROVENANCE shared.css row (release notes, Docs(plugins) entry). After the merge the catalog, the todo-watch band and the snapshot will list finished work as an open decision. The item's proposed_change also contradicts its own summary on banner-status ('move Loading ahead of Checks'), while the code correctly puts Loading last.
fix: Retire the item: run `todo_sync.py retire todo-5v8j`, then `todo_sync.py render`. List #331 as a close candidate, or close it, once this PR merges.
If any part is meant to stay open, clear `needs_decision` and `decision_question`, set the status to OPEN, and narrow the title and proposed_change to the remaining work.
Retire the item in this PR (`todo_sync.py retire todo-5v8j`, or the todo-edit retire flow), then re-render the snapshot. List #331 as a close candidate.
If the item has to stay open for a follow-up, set its status to the remaining work and drop the decision_question that this PR already answered.
Set the item's decision to the trim that shipped (needs_decision false, status OPEN or resolved) with `todo_sync.py inbox put --update`, then retire it with `todo_sync.py retire` once #331 closes.
Drop the item from this PR's catalog change and close #331 from the merge.
Retire todo-5v8j with `todo_sync.py retire` (citing the commits or #333), so the catalog counts drop back.
Or, if #331 stays open for follow-ups, update the item through the inbox: set status OPEN, clear needs_decision and decision_question, and narrow summary and proposed_change to the work that remains.

minor.summary:
README.md:42 introduces the new table with 'need no configuration', yet the check-runlogs row (README.md:47) names a skill that refuses with exit 1 while `runlogs.dir` is unset (defaults.json `runlogs.dir: null`; check-runlogs SKILL.md:22-27 tells the agent to show the key to add). Move check-runlogs out of this table into a row or note that names its `runlogs.dir` key.
Change the intro to 'need no configuration, except check-runlogs, which reads runlogs.dir (or takes --dir)', or add that note to the check-runlogs row.

minor.name: Requirements overstates which harness code needs pydantic, jsonschema and referencing
minor.summary: The new Requirements section (README.md:130-131) says Python 3.11 is needed 'for every harness hook and script, with pydantic>=2.1, jsonschema and referencing installed'. The same README says otherwise in two places: 'Commit, summary and worktree tooling need only the standard library' (README.md:450), and doctor is 'Standard library only, so it runs when pydantic, jsonschema or referencing are missing' (README.md:31). The arc-straps README also lists jsonschema as optional.
fix: Reword to: 'Python 3.11 or later for every harness hook and script; review, plan, TODO and schema-hook code also needs pydantic>=2.1, jsonschema and referencing (python -m pip install ...).'

minor.name: The harness_version key row names no consumer, and nothing reads the key
minor.summary: The new Configuration keys row (README.md:627) fills the 'Used by' column with 'the plugin version a pinned schemas_dir copy was synced from'. That reads as if harness checks pins against it. In fact config.py:207 and 354 only store `harness_version`, and no module or hook reads it. The `todo.snapshots.name_pattern` row (README.md:660) shows the table's convention for such a key: 'read by nothing'.
fix: Reword the row to 'informational, read by nothing: the plugin version a pinned schemas_dir copy was synced from, recorded by hand'.

minor.name: schemas README says TodoCatalog and DesignEvolutionCatalog keep sibling-path refs; neither has any
minor.summary:
The rewritten Catalog Schemas intro (plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:160) names `TodoCatalog` and `DesignEvolutionCatalog` as the standalone catalogs and then says 'Both keep sibling-path refs.' Every `$ref` in both files is a local `#/$defs/...` pointer. Only ConsumerAudit and Decompose reference a sibling file (SymbolCatalog.base). The sentence came from the removed CICDActionAudit wording and is now false for both catalogs it names.

Also (system_shape): The rewritten catalog intro (plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:160) names `TodoCatalog` and `DesignEvolutionCatalog` as the standalone catalogs, then says 'Both keep sibling-path refs.' Neither schema has a `$ref` to another file. Only ConsumerAudit.catalog.schema.json and Decompose.catalog.schema.json have non-`#` refs, the ones to SymbolCatalog.base. minor.name: Schema change step names plan_models.py and its drift test for Receipt and DesignEvolutionCatalog too
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:328 (rewritten in this PR) says `ActionPlan`, `Receipt` and `catalogs/DesignEvolutionCatalog` come from the models through gen_plan_schema.py, then says to 'change `harness_lib/plan_models.py` ... `tests/contract/test_plan_schema_generated.py` fails on drift' for all three. Receipt comes from receipt_models.py, DesignEvolutionCatalog from evolution_models.py, and both are checked by tests/contract/test_evolution_receipt_schema_generated.py, as the same README says at lines 138 and 200. A maintainer following step 1 would edit the wrong model file for those two schemas.

Also (system_shape): plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:328 (rewritten in this PR) says ActionPlan, Receipt and DesignEvolutionCatalog all come from gen_plan_schema.py, with the instruction 'change harness_lib/plan_models.py ... tests/contract/test_plan_schema_generated.py fails on drift'. Sections 11 (line 138) and DesignEvolution (line 200) of the same file say otherwise: Receipt comes from receipt_models.py, DesignEvolution from evolution_models.py, and their drift test is tests/contract/test_evolution_receipt_schema_generated.py. test_plan_schema_generated.py does not mention Receipt or DesignEvolution.
fix: Rewrite the parenthetical at schemas/README.md:328 per schema: plan_models.py (plan_enums.py for an enum) and test_plan_schema_generated.py for ActionPlan; receipt_models.py and evolution_models.py with test_evolution_receipt_schema_generated.py for Receipt and DesignEvolutionCatalog.

Reword step 1 to: 'ActionPlan, Receipt and catalogs/DesignEvolutionCatalog come from plan_models.py (plan_enums.py for an enum), receipt_models.py and evolution_models.py through python tools/gen_plan_schema.py; test_plan_schema_generated.py and test_evolution_receipt_schema_generated.py fail on drift'.

minor.name: parallel2 README adds --include-undeclared without saying what it lifts
minor.summary: The Stage row now shows `stage <lane> [--include-undeclared]`, but nothing in the README explains it. The cleanup row explains its new `--lane` flag. The stage prose at README.md:41-42 lists the refusals (a lane path unstaged, untracked or restaged since setup) but leaves out the refusal this flag lifts: the lane changed paths outside its declared files (parallel2.py:33-34; the flag's help at parallel2.py:676 says it also stages paths outside the lane's files). A reader of the README cannot tell when the flag applies.

minor.name: pr-review README says every refuter starts with init; only findings refuters do
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/skills/pr-review/README.md:16 reads '`-a`: one Workflow call, refuters start with `init`'. Code refuters (`adv_code`, `adv_code_<scope>`) do not run `init`: plugins/harness/agents/adversarial-reviewer.md:72-73 says 'A findings refuter reads the brief and then runs `init`', and the v1.0.0 notes (docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:184) say 'a findings refuter starts with `pr_review.py init`'.

Also (skill_package): The Phase 2 row (`-a`: one Workflow call, refuters start with `init`; refutations under `-a`) and the REFUTED paragraph (`every finding refuted in an -a run`) are the README's first and only uses of `-a`. The README has no invocation line and never says that `-a` is the adversarial run, in which refuter agents check each reviewer's findings. A reader who gets only this file sees a flag with no meaning.

Also (skill_package): The rewritten Phase 2, 3 and 5 rows run far past the padded header widths (`Driver command` is 29 characters wide; the new Phase 2 cell is about 75), while the untouched Phase 1 and 4 rows keep the old padding. The table renders correctly but is ragged in the raw file, which the rest of the README keeps aligned.
fix: Change README.md:16's cell to '`-a`: one Workflow call, findings refuters start with `init`'.

Add one sentence before or after the phase table, for example: "`-a` (adversarial) adds a findings refuter per reviewer slot; a refuter that refutes every finding of an issue closes it as `REFUTED` at `build`."
Or add an invocation line `/harness:pr-review PR [-a]` under the intro, with a one-line gloss of `-a`.
Re-pad the table at README.md:13-19 to the widest cell of each column, or shorten the Phase 2 cell (move the `-a` detail into the paragraph below the table) and re-pad.

minor.name: pr-sum README usage line omits --no-auto-title
minor.summary: The `--auto-title` row now says `--no-auto-title` turns the `auto_title` key off for one run, but the invocation line at README.md:13 still shows only `[--auto-title]`. SKILL.md's argument-hint lists `[--auto-title] [--no-auto-title]` and pr_sum.py's usage shows `[--auto-title | --no-auto-title]`, so the README synopsis is the one place in the package that hides the flag.
fix: Change `[--auto-title]` on README.md:13 to `[--auto-title | --no-auto-title]`, matching pr_sum.py's usage and SKILL.md's argument-hint.

minor.name: spawnInput builder is copied into two test files instead of shared
minor.summary:
plugins/parallel2-lanes/hooks/spawn.test.ts:57-60 and plugins/parallel2-lanes/hooks/band.test.tsx:70-73 define the same `spawnInput` builder (same field set, same defaults). Each docstring says 'a change to `AgentSpawnInput` edits both copies', so keeping them in step depends on a comment. The next engine bump that adds a required `AgentSpawnInput` field has to change both copies. The repo already has a shared, non-test helper module next to mod tests (plugins/todo-watch/hooks/testWorld.ts, imported by todo-watch's band.test.tsx), so a single copy is the established pattern.

Also (roast): `spawnInput` is defined twice, byte for byte, in spawn.test.ts and band.test.tsx. Both doc comments admit 'a change to `AgentSpawnInput` edits both copies'. The next engine type change is exactly what this PR just handled, and it will fix one copy and leave the other failing `validate --strict`. agent-watcher repeats the pattern: tracker.test.ts adds `BAND_PROPS` beside the identical `BAND.props` in band.test.tsx. The comment is a reminder; a shared helper is a guarantee.
fix: Move `spawnInput` into a new plugins/parallel2-lanes/hooks/testSpawn.ts (modeled on plugins/todo-watch/hooks/testWorld.ts), export it, import it in spawn.test.ts and band.test.tsx, and drop the 'edits both copies' sentence from both docstrings.

Move `spawnInput` into one helper module that both test files import (as they already import from `./lanes`), and drop the 'edits both copies' comments. Do the same for the AbovePrompt props in agent-watcher (one exported `BAND_PROPS` that band.test.tsx and tracker.test.ts both use).
If the engine's test kit cannot share a non-hook module, keep both copies and add a test asserting they are equal.

minor.name: Test comment hard-codes the CI engine pin
minor.summary: The todo-watch band test comment says 'CI pins 2.1.330'. The ci.yml comment tells the next pin raise to update the test files only if they fail to type-check, so this one will silently go stale. That leaves a comment explaining test behaviour against an engine CI no longer runs.
fix: Reword it to 'CI's pinned engine (ci.yml) stacks each plugin's band as its own part ...', keeping the 2.1.323 threshold, which is a fact about the engine and does not move.

minor.name: pyproject description omits the banner-status plugin
minor.summary: The new project description lists the harness plugin, arc-straps and the session mods, but the marketplace also ships the skill-only banner-status plugin (CLAUDE.md and README layout). The one-line summary of the marketplace is therefore incomplete at 1.0.0.
fix: Name banner-status in the description, e.g. 'Claude Code marketplace: the harness plugin (...), arc-straps, banner-status and the session mods'
Shorten the description to avoid enumerating plugins, e.g. 'Claude Code marketplace: harness, arc-straps, banner-status and session mods'

minor.name: Marketplace release version has three homes and no owner
minor.summary: README 'Versions' now says `metadata.version` in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` 'names the current one', and `pyproject.toml` also moves to 1.0.0. Neither the Releases section of CLAUDE.md, which every branch that bumps a plugin follows, nor any test says who moves these two numbers, or when. CLAUDE.md still has each branch suggest the next release only through `docs/RELEASES/v<X.Y.Z>.md`. The next release branch will follow that procedure and leave both fields at 1.0.0, and nothing will notice. A version field that nothing keeps current ends up wrong.
fix: Add one sentence to the CLAUDE.md Releases section: the branch that creates `docs/RELEASES/v<X.Y.Z>.md` also sets `metadata.version` in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `version` in `pyproject.toml` to X.Y.Z.

Also, or instead, add a contract test asserting that `metadata.version` equals the `pyproject.toml` version and the newest `docs/RELEASES/v*.md` file name (spelling those file names out so `tools/select_tests.py` selects it).
